Subject: Billing for September renewal — VAT / place-of-supply question

Hi Mateo,

We're getting close to our September renewal for the team licensing (annual), and our AP team raised a couple of questions around VAT and invoicing that I want to resolve before the renewal hits our PO workflow. High level:

- Our parent is UK-based (AuraCorp Ltd, VAT GB123456789). The subscription will be consumed by product teams across the UK and an India subsidiary (Aura India Pvt Ltd).
- Does Redwood invoice net (reverse-charge) to the UK entity if we provide the VAT number? Or do you need to invoice local VAT for the UK?
- If the Indian entity is paying or will be listed on the PO, do we need to expect any GST withholding at source from India?

I've attached our VAT certificate for the UK entity and a screenshot of the billing routing we use internally. For context, AP wants either: (a) Redwood issues net invoices to the UK entity under reverse-charge with VAT ID on the invoice; or (b) Redwood invoices UK VAT and we handle reclaim — but they prefer (a).

Can you confirm what documentation you need and what the invoice will look like (VAT line present or not, billing name on invoice) so we can route the PO correctly? We're hoping to finalize by Monday so the renewal billing can proceed.

Thanks — Alice

Subject: Re: Billing for September renewal — VAT / place-of-supply question

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear note and the certificate. Quick answers up front, then next steps:

- For B2B SaaS licensing: we generally apply reverse-charge (invoice net) when the supplied VAT ID is valid and the billing entity is outside Redwood's tax registration jurisdiction for the service. For UK customers post-Brexit, we will invoice net under reverse-charge to a UK business that provides a valid GB VAT number (your preference (a) is the typical path).
- If the paying party is your India subsidiary and the supply is consumed in India, there is a risk of GST withholding depending on the contracting/billing entity and local rules. If the UK entity contracts and we bill the UK entity, India withholding would normally not be applied.

What I need from you to finalize:
1) Confirm the exact legal entity to appear on the Redwood invoice (legal name + billing address + VAT/Tax ID).
2) Confirm which entity will execute payment (UK AP or Aura India).
3) Provide the VAT certificate you attached (good) and the registration number for any other billing entity (if India is to be billed we need CIN/PAN and GSTIN).
4) PO number if you require it on the invoice.

Operational notes / what the invoice will show:
- Invoice net of VAT with a line: "Reverse charge — domestic recipient to account for VAT" and your VAT number included.
- We can include a note referencing the place-of-supply as "United Kingdom" for clarity.
- We will not collect UK VAT if reverse-charge is applied.

I've looped in Vanessa from Billing Ops to confirm the mechanics for multi-entity deals and to propose a short MAP (mutual action plan) so we hit your Monday deadline.

Proposed MAP:
- Today (Fri): You confirm billing entity + payer + PO number (if available).
- Mon 09/21: Redwood issues preliminary invoice (net), includes VAT ID and reverse-charge language.
- Payment due per standard terms (Net30) to the entity on the invoice.

If for any reason the India entity must pay and withhold GST at source, we'll need to capture 10%/2% (example numbers — final rates will depend on classification) and provide withholding certificates so you can claim set-off. That is not our default flow, so please flag early if you expect India AP to interact.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez

Hi Alice,

Quick operational add from Billing Ops:
- We can issue a net invoice (reverse-charge) to AuraCorp Ltd (GB123456789) provided the VAT number validates in the UK VIES/GB registry and we have a copy of the certificate on file. The invoice will show zero VAT charged and include the mandatory reverse-charge statement.
- If you need the invoice to show a UK VAT line (option b), we will need to be registered in the UK for VAT collection and that would change pricing/collection timing — not ideal for your stated preference.
- For India GST: if payment is directly made by Aura India Pvt Ltd and local law requires withholding, their AP will withhold at the statutory rate and we will issue a receipt/witness to the withholding (Form/Certificate) so you can claim credit. We will also accept a self-billing agreement if your AP requires it (I attached our template).

Action items from our side:
- I'll run the VAT number through validation Monday and update the HubSpot deal.
- If payment is coming from India, send the payer details (GSTIN + AP contact). We will set up a withholding tracking field on the invoice and provide a withholding certificate after payment.
